answer: In this PoA design, continuous identity verification requires a Wesolowski VDF: a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings with a compact, efficiently checked proof. Simulating many identities does not multiply progress, because each clone must complete its own non-parallelizable sequence; GPUs can run separate instances, but cannot shorten any instance’s physical wall-clock delay. Thus a mirror key, hollow clone, or beacon-led swarm cannot cheaply manufacture independent agents.
